summary: In this story, a boy and his cousin follow an old hand-drawn map from their grandfather's attic to a hidden family chest in the hills.
introduce: Show the title “The Treasure Map” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: something easy to notice that helps you know where you are
a piece of information that helps solve a mystery
an old object passed down in a family for many years

challengeTerms.def: a family member who lived a long time before you
to figure out the meaning of something that is hard to read or understand
to dig carefully to uncover something buried

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that old family objects are more interesting than new things you can buy in a store? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how the old map helped Faisal and Noura discover something important about their family.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review landmark, clue, and heirloom, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses ancestor, decipher, and excavate to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
